title: The Answer After a Week
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、法令、医療制度、実証結果ではない。登録台帳は制作来歴確認用。

sentences.en: At an imaginary high school, a teacher asks her students to explain a scientific concept immediately after reading a chapter and discovers that almost everyone can reproduce the main definition with impressive accuracy.
sentences.ja: 架空の高校で教師は章を読んだ直後に科学概念を説明させ、ほぼ全員が主な定義を驚くほど正確に再現できることに気づく。

sentences.en: The students are pleased with their performance and several conclude that the remaining study time should be devoted to entirely unfamiliar topics rather than reviewing what they have apparently mastered.
sentences.ja: 生徒は成績に満足し、既に習得したように見える内容の復習より残りの時間を全く未知の題材に費やすべきと考える者もいる。

sentences.en: A week later, however, the teacher presents a new situation in which the same concept is relevant without explicitly identifying the chapter from which the necessary information was originally obtained.
sentences.ja: しかし一週間後、必要情報が元のどの章から得られたか明示せず同じ概念が関連する新状況を提示する。

sentences.en: Some students recognize the relationship immediately, while others struggle to recall the definition or discover that they cannot explain why the concept applies to the unfamiliar circumstances.
sentences.ja: 関係をすぐ認識する者もいれば定義の想起に苦労したり未知の状況に概念が適用できる理由を説明できないと気づく者もいる。

sentences.en: The teacher distinguishes several possible difficulties rather than assuming that the students have all experienced the same kind of failure in the interval between the two classroom activities.
sentences.ja: 二つの活動の間に全員が同じ種類の失敗を経験したと想定せず複数の困難を区別する。

sentences.en: A student who cannot recall the relevant definition without looking at the original text may need a different kind of practice from someone who remembers it accurately but cannot recognize when it is useful.
sentences.ja: 原文を見ずに関連定義を思い出せない生徒には正確に覚えていても使用場面を認識できない生徒とは異なる練習が必要かもしれない。

sentences.en: Another learner might identify the appropriate concept yet lack the vocabulary required to communicate an explanation in a form that another person can understand.
sentences.ja: 別の学習者は適切な概念を特定できても他者が理解できる形で説明する語彙が不足しているかもしれない。

sentences.en: The teacher explains that the original assessment provided information about a particular performance under particular conditions, not a comprehensive demonstration of every aspect of the students' understanding.
sentences.ja: 元の評価は特定条件下の特定成績についての情報を提供したのであり理解の全側面を包括的に示したのではないと説明する。

sentences.en: For subsequent lessons, the students prepare short questions that require them to retrieve relevant information before consulting their notes and to explain how the information relates to a new example.
sentences.ja: その後の授業で、生徒はノートを見る前に関連情報を思い出し新しい例との関連を説明する短い問いを用意する。

sentences.en: They compare their answers with the original materials afterward, paying particular attention to details that they had omitted or relationships that they had mistakenly assumed to be correct.
sentences.ja: 後で元資料と回答を比較し、省いた詳細や正しいと誤って想定した関係に特に注意する。

sentences.en: The teacher also provides opportunities to revisit the material at different times so that students can examine whether their ability to use it extends beyond the immediate context of a single lesson.
sentences.ja: 一つの授業直後の文脈を超えて内容を使えるか調べるため異なる時点で内容を見直す機会も提供する。

sentences.en: The fictional exercise is designed to illustrate several kinds of learning goals rather than demonstrate the effectiveness of a particular revision schedule through genuine experimental evidence.
sentences.ja: 架空の練習は実際の実験的証拠で特定の復習日程の効果を示すのでなく複数の学習目標を例示するよう設計される。

sentences.en: During a discussion about examination preparation, the students notice that reading their notes can create a satisfying impression of familiarity even when they have not yet attempted to answer a question independently.
sentences.ja: 試験準備の議論で、生徒は独力で問いに答えようとしていなくてもノートを読むとなじみがあるという満足な印象を生み得ると気づく。

sentences.en: One student describes her surprise when she discovers that a paragraph she recognizes immediately is considerably more difficult to reconstruct after the book has been closed.
sentences.ja: 見ればすぐ分かる段落も本を閉じると再構成がかなり難しいと知った驚きを一人が語る。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the teacher does not suggest abandoning reading or dismissing familiarity as worthless, since understanding an initial explanation remains an important part of acquiring new knowledge.
sentences.ja: それでも最初の説明を理解することは新知識獲得の重要部分なので、読書をやめたり親近感を無価値と見なしたりするよう提案しない。

sentences.en: Instead, she encourages students to distinguish the purposes of different activities and to select practice methods that address the difficulties they have actually encountered.
sentences.ja: 代わりに活動の目的を区別し実際に直面した困難に対処する練習法を選ぶよう促す。

sentences.en: An educational activity may feel successful because it produces an immediate and reassuring result, but that result does not necessarily answer the questions that matter at a later stage of learning.
sentences.ja: 教育活動は即座の安心できる結果を生むため成功と感じられても、結果が後の学習段階で重要な問いに答えるとは限らない。

sentences.en: Useful feedback identifies the circumstances under which a learner can access, explain, and apply knowledge, rather than treating understanding as a single condition that is either present or absent.
sentences.ja: 有益な助言は理解を有無だけの状態と扱わず学習者が知識にアクセスし説明し適用できる事情を特定する。

sentences.en: The distinction helps students decide when familiar material deserves further attention even though its appearance in a textbook no longer produces any apparent difficulty.
sentences.ja: この区別は教科書で見ても困難を感じなくなった内容がさらに注意に値する時期を判断する助けになる。

sentences.en: For these fictional students, the answer produced after a week becomes an opportunity to investigate what their earlier success actually demonstrated and what it left unresolved.
sentences.ja: 架空の生徒にとって一週間後の答えは以前の成功が実際に何を示し何を未解決のまま残したか調べる機会になる。

vocabulary.definition: how well an activity is completed
actually what it claims to be

options: The accuracy of students' immediate definitions.
Their ability to solve every unfamiliar problem.
Their ability to write new chapters.

questions.prompt: Why does the later task differ from the first?
options: It uses material from an unrelated subject.
It allows students to copy every definition.
It requires recognizing relevance without an explicit cue.
It asks only for the same words in the same context.

questions.prompt: What distinction does the teacher make?
options: Reading versus all forms of learning.
Failure to recall versus failure to recognize applicability.
Fast learners versus slow learners only.

questions.prompt: Why was the first assessment insufficient?
options: It contained no useful evidence whatsoever.
It required too much vocabulary for everyone.
It established all students had mastered the topic.
It measured performance under limited conditions.

questions.prompt: What do students do before consulting notes?
Why revisit material at different times?
options: Investigate whether knowledge remains usable beyond one lesson.
Guarantee every student learns at an identical rate.
Prove an exact revision schedule is best.
Replace the need for initial explanation.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる時点での利用可能性を調べる。

options: She had never seen the paragraph before.
Reading made her forget every word.
A familiar paragraph was hard to reconstruct without the book.

questions.prompt: Why does the teacher retain reading as an activity?
options: Reading is sufficient for every learning goal.
Initial comprehension serves a valuable purpose.
questions.explanation_ja: 初期理解には価値がある。

options: Immediate correct answers prove durable mastery.
A single assessment can reveal every aspect of understanding.
Evaluate learning through several kinds of performance and choose practice that addresses actual difficulties.
questions.explanation_ja: 複数の学習目標を評価。

grammar.focus: from someone who remembers it accurately

grammar.explanation_ja: 分詞構文で比較時の行動を補足。

grammar.focus: rather than treating understanding as a single condition

paraphrases.rewrite: Some students want to move on because they believe they have already mastered the material.

paraphrases.source: A student who cannot recall the relevant definition without looking at the original text may need a different kind of practice from someone who remembers it accurately but cannot recognize when it is useful.
paraphrases.rewrite: Recall difficulties and application difficulties can require different practice.

paraphrases.source: They compare their answers with the original materials afterward, paying particular attention to details that they had omitted or relationships that they had mistakenly assumed to be correct.
paraphrases.rewrite: They compare answers and focus on omissions and mistaken assumptions.

paraphrases.source: Useful feedback identifies the circumstances under which a learner can access, explain, and apply knowledge, rather than treating understanding as a single condition that is either present or absent.
paraphrases.rewrite: Feedback should reveal multiple aspects of knowledge use instead of classifying understanding as simply present or absent.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 理解は一つの状態でない。

discourse.role_ja: 直後と一週間後の対比。
一律の失敗と異なる困難の対比。
親近感の限界と読書の価値。

cloze.explanation_ja: 包括的な理解の証明ではない。
